contraindications: History of tendon disorders related to quinolone use
cautions: exposure to excessive sunlight and UV radiation should be avoided during treatment and for 48 hours after stopping treatment
children or adolescents (arthropathy has developed in weight-bearing joints in young animals ) (in children)

Quinolones cause arthropathy in the weight-bearing joints of immature animals and are therefore generally not recommended in children and growing adolescents. However, the significance of this effect in humans is uncertain and in some specific circumstances use of ciprofloxacin may be justified in children.
Known (or at risk of) perforated tympanic membrane

bradycardia (risk factor for QT interval prolongation)
congenital long QT syndrome (risk factor for QT interval prolongation)
electrolyte disturbances (risk factor for QT interval prolongation)
ensure adequate fluid intake (risk of crystalluria)
heart failure with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (risk factor for QT interval prolongation)
history of symptomatic arrhythmias (risk factor for QT interval prolongation)

interactions.description: Manufacturer advises avoid concurrent administration of dairy products and mineral-fortified drinks with oral ciprofloxacin due to reduced exposure.

renalConsiderations: Give 250–500 mg every 12 hours if eGFR 30–60 mL/minute/1.73 m 2 (every 24 hours if eGFR less than 30 mL/minute/1.73 m 2 ).
Give (200 mg over 30 minutes), 200–400 mg every 12 hours if eGFR 30–60 mL/minute/ 1.73m 2 (every 24 hours if eGFR less than 30 mL/ minute/1.73 m 2 ).
Reduce dose if estimated glomerular filtration rate less than 30 mL/minute/1.73 m 2 —consult product literature.
pregnancyBreastfeeding: Avoid in pregnancy—shown to cause arthropathy in animal studies; safer alternatives are available.
UKHSA advises a single dose of ciprofloxacin may be used for prevention of secondary case of meningococcal disease.

practicalPoints: Manufacturer advises discard any ampoules remaining 8 days after opening the pouch.

Patients and their carers should be advised to stop fluoroquinolone treatment at the first signs of a serious musculoskeletal, neurological or psychiatric side effect and to contact their doctor immediately. The MHRA has produced a patient advice sheet on fluoroquinolones and serious adverse reactions affecting tendons, muscles, joints, and nerves, which should be provided to patients and their carers: https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/65aa9125c69eea0010883840/FQ_Patient_Information_Sheet_-_TO_PUBLISH.pdf .
May impair performance of skilled tasks (e.g. driving); effects enhanced by alcohol.
